title: Machine-Checked 2D Euclidean Distance Kernel and Exact-Q Polygon Mean-Width, Similarity, and Budget Certificates
abstract: Inspired by OpenAI's November 24, 2026 preprint embedding planar Euclidean mean width W(S) = P/2, collinear copy insertion, contraction monotonicity, and borrowed-wire margins into Strassen's asymptotic spectrum of tensors, we present an explicitly scoped, standalone, zero-floating-point verification stack pairing two layers. Layer 1 (AsymptoticSpectrumGeometry.lean, Lean 4.35.0; 18 theorems, 0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice, 0 warnings) proves exact 2D integer Euclidean geometry laws—Euclid's Pythagorean parametrization, translation/homogeneity invariance, Lagrange's 2D Cauchy-Schwarz, rational-length triangle inequality (with r_u, r_v >= 0), segment-restricted collinear zero-excess (with 0 <= t <= k and r >= 0), and 2D scaled-rotation (similarity) isometry and contraction monotonicity—together with elementary integer/list algebraic projections (distributivity, Nat power laws, list-sum monotonicity, and linear margin contradictions). Layer 2 (SPEC-GEOM-CERT-1.0, pure-stdlib Python Fraction) provides a fully specified four-mode auditor that replays 16 canonical exact-Q certificates in 0.071-0.313 ms (auditing global strict CCW polygon convexity and W(S) = P/2, collinear vs. exterior triangle gaps, 2D similarity contractions, and finite arithmetic barrier checks), cross-checks W(S) = P/2 against 4096-angle Cauchy-Crofton projection integration, and rejects 58/58 live adversarial forgeries.
